subject: Pen test scope: tenant isolation, KMS ownership, and asset inventory
messages:
From: security@acmerobotics.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Hi Tessa / Laura,

Thanks for working with us. We're preparing to run an external penetration test against the stack supporting Acme's integration. Before we schedule the vendor, we need confirmation on a few scope points so our procurement and legal teams can sign off. High-level questions: 

- Which hosting variants will Redwood include in the pen test you provide to customers by default? Specifically: Hosted (shared), Dedicated (reserved pools), Private (VPC-deployed control plane), and on-prem installer.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, who is responsible for KMS/CMK ownership and rotation? Does Redwood ever have access to customer CMKs or plaintext model artifacts?
- What assets are considered in-scope for Redwood's standard pen test? Examples: control-plane API endpoints, model-serving hosts, KV cache/network-attached caches, object storage (model artifacts), telemetry/metrics endpoints, and compilation/kernel binaries.
- Can you provide a redacted copy of the most recent pen test report for a similar customer (we understand IP will be removed)?

Attached is a short questionnaire from our security team (acme-pt-questions.xlsx) and an inventory template (asset_inventory_acme.csv).

Goal: get a definitive in-scope list and who owns what by 21-Mar so we can book the vendor for the week of 04-Apr.

Appreciate any clarifications.

—Jacob Brown
Security Engineer | Acme Robotics
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: jacob.brown@acmerobotics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (security) and Aditya (infra) to provide the technical boundary and KMS details.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Aditya/Laura to reply with an initial in-scope asset matrix and KMS responsibilities by EOD 2028-03-16.
- We'll produce a redacted pen test report and a short coverage summary by 2028-03-18.
- If anything remains unclear, schedule a 30-minute call (I can host Tue/Wed next week).

I'm attaching our internal pen-test checklist (redwood-pt-checklist.pdf) and an inventory template we prefer filled out if you want us to ingest it directly.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, jacob.brown@acmerobotics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-15T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Jacob / Tessa — technical clarifications below; I'm keeping answers concise so you can feed them back to procurement.

1) Hosted (shared):
- In-scope: Redwood-managed control plane endpoints (API gateway, tenant routing) and the shared serving fleet that processes multi-tenant requests.
- Out-of-scope: customer data at rest tied to other customers; Redwood will ensure tenant isolation at application layer.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools):
- In-scope: the hosts/pods in the Redwood-managed reserved pool that are allocated to Acme (host OS, container runtime, serving process).
- Out-of-scope: anything the customer deploys into their own VPC/network that is not part of the reserved Redwood-managed pool.
- KMS/keys: Dedicated supports customer-managed CMKs via cloud KMS (customer provides key ID). Redwood never has access to plaintext decrypted by the customer's CMK. We do operate short-lived service credentials for orchestration that do not expose CMK material.

3) Private (VPC / customer-managed control plane) and On‑Prem:
- Private (VPC): we typically deploy a Redwood control plane component into the customer's VPC; in that model, the customer controls the network boundary. In-scope for Redwood's report are the Redwood-supplied components we deploy and maintain in that VPC (we'll enumerate those).
- On‑prem: generally out-of-scope for Redwood-run external pen tests unless explicitly negotiated; the customer-run environment and underlying infra are the customer's responsibility. For on-prem installs we provide a recommended static scope and require the customer to authorize the vendor's access to those hosts.

4) Specific assets to call out:
- KV cache (in-memory / distributed): in-scope if it is network-accessible from outside the tenant VPC or if it exposes tenant-level interfaces. Ephemeral caches that live only on host memory and not reachable via external network are typically out-of-scope.
- Model artifacts in object storage: for Hosted/Dedicated, Redwood controls the storage bucket; for Private/on-prem, the customer may control it. Access control and encryption at-rest are applied.
- Compilation/kernel binaries: these are part of the Redwood runtime and are in-scope for our internal tests; we'll include them in the scope summary for Acme.

5) Report redaction: we can provide a redacted PDF that removes any customer-specific attack chains and internal IPs. We'll include a mapping of CVEs and remediation status.

I'll attach an asset list template (I filled a few rows) as asset_inventory_acme.csv. Let me know if you'd like deeper segmentation (network, host, app, data).

—Aditya Rao
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: jacob.brown@acmerobotics.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-16T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Thanks Aditya — that helps. A couple follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the asset template: 

- Can you confirm whether the KV cache exposes any metrics endpoints (Prometheus / statsd) that could be scraped from the public control plane? If so, those endpoints should be in-scope.
- For Dedicated: does Redwood log model inputs or outputs for debugging? If logs exist, where are they stored and who has access? We need to ensure logs do not contain PII or robot control sequences that are considered sensitive.
- We have two open vulnerabilities (CVEs) from a previous internal scan that we'd like Redwood to confirm status on: CVE-2026-4488 and CVE-2027-1102. Are these in your remediation backlog?

Also attaching a short list from our vendor (PentestOps) with probing rules (acme-pt-questions.xlsx).

—Jacob
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: jacob.brown@acmerobotics.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-18T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Jacob — quick status update and answers to your follow-ups.

- Metrics endpoints: The KV cache does expose internal metrics over a metrics endpoint but it is behind our control plane and not reachable from the public internet. For Hosted deployments our control plane authenticates and authorizes metrics scrapers; we'll include the exact endpoint and auth model in the scope doc. If PentestOps wants it tested we can make the endpoint available through a temporary, scoped access path.

- Logging: Redwood collects short-lived debug logs for inference jobs in Dedicated; these logs are stored in a customer-isolated bucket when customer opts in. By default we redact user inputs that match configured PII rules; we can share our logging retention and redaction policy. Access to those buckets is limited to the Ops SRE group and is audited.

- CVE status:
  - CVE-2026-4488: patched in runtime v2027.11.2, rollout completed to Dedicated and Hosted fleets on 2028-02-10.
  - CVE-2027-1102: identified; mitigation in progress. Targeted remediation and deploy planned for 2028-03-25; currently in validation for Canary hosts.

What we'll provide by 2028-03-18:
- A redacted pen test PDF (redacted-pt-report-acme-2027.pdf) with attack surface mapping and confirmation of which Redwood-managed components are covered.
- A one-page in-scope asset matrix that enumerates control plane, serving hosts, storage, caches, and telemetry endpoints for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- A remediation timeline for identified CVEs (we've opened JIRA SEC-4321 and linked it above).

If the Acme team is comfortable, let's schedule a 30-minute triage call the week of 2028-03-21 to walk PentestOps through temporary access for any endpoints they request. I can join with Aditya and Rishi.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jacob.brown@acmerobotics.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, pentest@redteam.io
Date: 2028-03-21T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Pen test request & scoping questions for Acme deployment

Laura / Tessa — that timeline works. Please go ahead and send the redacted report and the one-page asset matrix; we'll review and confirm the vendor scope. I've proposed Tuesday 2028-03-28 10:00 AM ET for the triage call — invite to follow.

Thanks for the CVE updates and the clear ownership notes on KMS. One final ask before the call: can you add a line in the asset matrix clarifying whether model weights stored in Dedicated buckets are encrypted with customer CMKs (yes/no) and whether Redwood will ever have plaintext access during model load or runtime? That will speed our procurement review.

—Jacob
